reading.locator: Review and Validation and threat-model maintenance across the SDLC. Pair with CSF 2.0 Govern outcomes for ownership and supply-chain decisions.

assignment.title: A change-impact security review
instructions: Propose a fictional offline export feature and one new dependency for the lab service.
Update the data-flow model, retention/deletion policy, permission matrix and dependency evidence without building a real external integration.
Record which existing tests must change and which security claims remain unsupported.
acceptanceCriteria: Export authorization and retention are explicitly reviewed.
A supplier update is tied to identity, provenance and maintenance evidence.
Design intent is not labelled as a control that has been implemented and tested.

questions.prompt: A new data export endpoint requires what?
choices: Reuse the old read permission without evaluating bulk disclosure
A fresh boundary, authorization and privacy review
Approve on transport encryption alone without reviewing retention and ownership
questions.answer: A fresh boundary, authorization and privacy review
questions.explanation: Export changes how much data can cross a boundary and how it may be retained. Existing login does not establish safe scope.

questions.prompt: How should an untested architecture claim appear in a handover?
questions.answer: As a proposed or unverified control with its assumptions and required verification, not as demonstrated protection.
questions.explanation: Evidence quality depends on honest separation of what is intended, implemented and actually checked.

reviewPrompts: What new trust assumption did this change introduce?

modules.title: 12. Defended-service capstone and operational handover
modules.description: Demonstrate layered mechanisms, realistic residual risk and recovery in a wholly authorized synthetic environment.

lessons.title: Deliver an evidence-backed defensive system
objectives: Integrate identity, cryptographic, OS/network, application/data and delivery controls.
Map each protection to a threat, an enforcement mechanism and a reproducible test.

topics.title: Layered assurance
details: Controls should have independent purposes and known failure boundaries.
A minimal well-tested service is preferable to an unverified stack of products.

topics.title: Acceptance
details: Review includes negative cases, outages and cleanup.
Residual risk and unsupported hardware features remain visible.

reading.locator: Existing hosted ASVS 5.0.0: revisit the exact requirement IDs selected in l19 for authentication, sessions, authorization, API and data protection. Do not claim coverage of untested requirements.

assignment.title: Capstone: a defended synthetic notes service
instructions: Deliver an owned loopback/host-only service with two synthetic tenants, maintained authentication, revocable sessions, resource-level authorization and scoped local TLS.
Apply least-privilege OS/database roles, allowed network flows, bounded API validation, safe output handling and a dependency/provenance manifest.
Add redacted logging, labelled detections, dummy-secret rotation and a tested backup/restore path. Use only benign authorized test cases.
Package the threat model, scoped ASVS/CSF matrix, architecture decisions, residual-risk register and a clean reproducibility/teardown procedure.
deliverables: Local runnable service and synthetic fixture pack
Scope/authorization statement and complete cleanup instructions
acceptanceCriteria: No real accounts, credentials, public targets, harmful payloads, evasion or production settings are involved.
Owner, anonymous, stale-session and invalid-input tests enforce the declared boundaries.
TLS trust checks, least-privilege roles and network flow restrictions have reproducible evidence.
Artifact provenance, secret rotation and sensitive-log exclusions are checked.
Detection cases include benign negatives and documented gaps.
A restored service preserves data integrity and owner isolation.
Unsupported controls and residual risks are labelled; no certification or complete-security claim is made.

questions.prompt: Which capstone result is acceptable to report?
choices: Every component meets the standard because selected requirements passed
Local test success proves the application cannot have unknown defects
Scoped controls passed named tests, with these residual risks
questions.answer: Scoped controls passed named tests, with these residual risks
questions.explanation: Security evidence is bounded by scope, time, assumptions and test coverage. Professional Practice does not award certification.

questions.prompt: What should block handover even if the application appears functional?
questions.answer: Examples include a cross-owner data leak, exposed real secret, unverified restore, disabled TLS validation or unresolved critical permission mismatch.
questions.explanation: The service must meet its stated safety and protection contract, not only return a successful page.

reviewPrompts: Can every 'secure' claim be replaced with a specific tested mechanism?

lessons.title: Defend the architecture through an incident and recovery review
objectives: Run a reviewer-selected benign failure drill and verify recovery.
Hand over limitations, risk owners and operating procedures clearly.

topics.title: Operational acceptance
details: A peer or delayed blind self-review chooses an access denial and recovery case.
The reviewer verifies restored authorization as well as data availability.

topics.title: Handover
details: Open risks, source versions and next-review triggers remain attached to the artifact.
Safe teardown removes dummy secrets and restores the isolated lab boundary.

reading.locator: Rev. 3 Recover and improvement recommendations in the linked full publication; use measured recovery evidence and tracked corrective actions.

assignment.title: Final evidence gate: a recoverable security architecture
instructions: Give the reviewer the clean bundle and let them select a synthetic owner-denial case, log-sink interruption and backup-restoration scenario.
Measure detection/response/recovery timing, reconcile restored records and rerun permissions/TLS/session checks.
Deliver a challenge-response memo, unresolved-risk handover and teardown record. Simulate incident effects with fixture changes only; never create a real intrusion.
deliverables: Reviewer-selected drill transcript and measured results
acceptanceCriteria: The chosen denial and restoration cases reproduce from documented commands.
Recovery preserves ownership, logging and session-revocation behavior.
Target misses and open findings are explicit with owners and next checks.
Dummy secrets, scoped test trust and temporary lab resources are cleaned up without affecting shared systems.

questions.prompt: After restoring records, what must still be checked?
choices: Authorization, session state, integrity and operational controls
Only whether the restored row count matches, regardless of ownership
Only whether the backup checksum is valid, without exercising the restored service
questions.answer: Authorization, session state, integrity and operational controls
questions.explanation: Recovery must restore the intended security properties, not just availability of some files.

questions.prompt: What belongs in an honest final security handover?
questions.answer: Scope, tested versions, mechanisms, reproducible evidence, failed or untested cases, residual-risk owners and review/recovery procedures.
questions.explanation: A defensible handover lets the next operator understand both the protections and their limits.

reviewPrompts: Which residual risk should the next operator understand first?

limitations: Defensive practice only in owned or explicitly authorized isolated labs using synthetic users, data and traffic. No real-target intrusion, credential harvesting, harmful payloads, evasion, public scanning or production/security-setting changes.
Professional Practice is a learning level, not a professional certification, qualification, regulatory compliance claim or guarantee that a system has no vulnerabilities.

Use maintained cryptographic/authentication libraries. Never invent production cryptography, disable TLS verification or alter the host-wide trust store, firmware, real keys or firewall for these exercises.

All required readings and lecture viewing are free. No cloud account, billing, paid lab, certificate, textbook or special hardware purchase is needed. Hardware controls can be assessed through a clearly labelled documentation-backed design when unavailable in the lab.
The ASVS reader reuses the existing approved PDF, checksum and per-book consent behavior. Other standards, diagrams and recordings remain external official links and are not rehosted.
Historical MIT, cryptography and firewall sources teach mechanisms; current NIST identity/incident guidance and maintained platform documentation govern contemporary configuration choices.
Common Foundation, SDE and other shared lessons retain original progress IDs. Prerequisites guide understanding while previews stay open; extra-topic completion remains separate from core progress.
